summary: Saparmurat Niyazov, Soviet party boss turned president for life of Turkmenistan from 1990 to 2006, built a golden personality cult, imposed his book the Ruhnama as scripture, jailed and tortured dissidents and ruled by whim.

evidence.note: born 1940 near Ashgabat; father killed in the war, family lost in the 1948 earthquake
made Turkmen party first secretary in 1985, then sole candidate after 1990 independence
courting the Clinton administration, pipeline deals and the White House visit
about 20,000 political prisoners; a former detainee describes torture methods
Ruhnama placed in mosques and schools, required for exams and driving tests
ambassador Shikhmuradov defects; 2002 motorcade attack used to crush dissidents
chief mufti arrested after objecting to the Ruhnama sharing place with the Koran
dies of heart failure at the end of 2006; successor mentioned only briefly

notes: Guest is named David Bell in the descriptions; the transcript's speech recognition garbles the name. Germany (heart surgery) and Afghanistan (Taliban pipeline, US airbase deal) mentioned too briefly for the setting. The Ruhnama casts Niyazov as a prophet, but the regime is a personality cult, not a cult organization, so cults-new-religions was not used.
